headline: Far-Right Israeli Minister Urges Nightly Killings in Gaza, Threatening Regional Stability
deck: Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for the killing of 30 to 40 Palestinians in Gaza each night, escalating his incendiary rhetoric and drawing international condemnation.
body: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, a far-right figure in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, called for the nightly killing of 30 to 40 people in Gaza during a podcast appearance this week. The remarks were reported by CBS News, the Financial Times, and Middle East Eye, placing Ben Gvir’s inflammatory comments at the center of regional discourse. His role as a senior Israeli official amplifies the gravity of the statement, which has drawn sharp criticism from diplomats and analysts alike. The suggestion comes amid sustained military operations in Gaza that have already claimed tens of thousands of lives since October 7, according to Gaza health authorities.

Ben Gvir made the comments on a podcast, according to ITVX, where he framed the killing of Gazans as a necessary response to what he described as an existential threat. His assertion that Gazans ‘are not even people’ was cited by CBS News as part of a broader pattern of dehumanizing rhetoric that has defined parts of the Israeli political discourse since the war began. The statement was made in the context of escalating tensions, including a months-long blockade, intense bombardment, and repeated ground incursions into the besieged enclave.

The call for systematic killings from a sitting minister has raised alarms about Israel’s conduct in Gaza and its broader implications for regional stability. Analysts warn that such rhetoric risks normalizing mass violence and could further isolate Israel diplomatically, particularly in the Arab world. The International Court of Justice is already weighing accusations of genocide against Israel, a case that gained momentum after South Africa’s initial filing in December.

Meanwhile, the diplomatic fallout has already begun. A UAE billionaire publicly questioned whether normalization with Israel remains viable in the wake of Ben Gvir’s remarks. The comment, reported by Middle East Eye, signals growing unease among Arab states that had previously sought to engage with Israel despite the ongoing conflict. The UAE, which normalized relations with Israel in 2020 as part of the Abraham Accords, now faces pressure to reassess its position.

The timing of Ben Gvir’s comments is particularly sensitive, arriving as ceasefire negotiations remain stalled and humanitarian conditions in Gaza deteriorate. Over 35,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since October, according to Gaza health officials, with entire neighborhoods reduced to rubble and famine conditions reported in the north. The UN has warned of a man-made famine if aid deliveries are not significantly increased.

Ben Gvir’s rhetoric is not isolated. He has long been a polarizing figure in Israeli politics, known for his ultranationalist views and provocative statements. His party, Otzma Yehudit, advocates for Jewish supremacy and the annexation of the West Bank. His appointment as National Security Minister last year was met with widespread condemnation from human rights organizations and foreign governments.

The international community has reacted with outrage. The European Union, United Nations, and several Arab states have all issued statements condemning Ben Gvir’s remarks. The US State Department, while maintaining its support for Israel’s right to self-defense, has also expressed concern over inflammatory rhetoric from Israeli officials that could undermine prospects for peace.

Ben Gvir’s call for nightly killings in Gaza is a stark reminder of how deeply the conflict has eroded norms of human dignity and international law. His dehumanization of Palestinians mirrors tactics used in other conflicts to justify mass violence, and it risks embedding such rhetoric into the fabric of Israeli governance. The fact that such a senior official can make such statements without immediate repercussions underscores the impunity that has characterized this war.

"They're not even people," Ben Gvir said, a phrase that encapsulates the moral collapse at the heart of this conflict. The statement was reported by CBS News and reflects a broader pattern of dehumanization that has been used to justify the destruction of Gaza. Human rights organizations have long warned that such rhetoric paves the way for atrocities.

The question now is whether Israel’s allies will act to rein in Ben Gvir’s rhetoric or continue to shield his government from accountability. The UAE billionaire’s comments suggest that even traditional partners are questioning the cost of engagement with a government that includes figures like Ben Gvir. For now, the nightly killings he proposed remain a chilling possibility, one that could further destabilize an already volatile region.
